newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares rise but end under 3,700 barrier.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares rise but end under 3,700 barrier.

text.p: 1430 GMT - Swiss shares ended slightly higher in moderate volume but below a barrier of 3,700 points on the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI), despite edging higher during the day.
Profit taking and a weak Wall Street opening led to late losses. But traders said the market was ready to tackle the 3,700 line in the next few days.
A Swiss National Bank discount rate cut to 1.0 percent from 1.5 percent did little to enliven the market.
* The SMI ended up 0.05 percent, or 1.8 points, to 3,699.5.
* All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) firmed 3.88 points, or 0.16 percent, to 2,374.67 points.
* Shares of insurer Zurich, which led the actives list, jumped more than two percent to 344. Zurich said its half-year net profit rose 32.7 percent to 576.4 million francs.
* Insurer Winterthur added one franc to 775 while Swiss Re slid 10 francs to 1,314.
* Industrials mostly edged up in line with the market. Roche certificates ended lower after a firmer bias during most of the day, giving up 15 francs to 9,140.
* Banks were generally lower. UBS bearer shares and SBC edged down 0.42 percent each to 1,185 francs and 239,25 francs, respectively. CS Holding were unchanged at 123 francs.

* Shares of Swiss engineering group Sulzer yielded 1.7 percent to 699 francs after announcing 1996 group net profit was likely to be lower than 1995 due to a $73 million fine imposed by a U.S. appeals court in connection with a patent suit.
Sulzer said it had expected lower damages if it lost the case and had therefore set aside a provision of 45 million Swiss francs ($35.9 million), which now have to be topped off.
* Second-tier Saurer continued its recent upward move.
